title: Black Holes
objective: After this level you can explain what a black hole is and how one forms.
summary: A black hole is where gravity is so strong nothing escapes. Stellar ones form when very massive stars collapse.

cards.headline: A place where escape velocity is faster than light.
Gravity wins
cards.body: A black hole is a region of space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape. Stellar black holes form when the core of a very massive star collapses at the end of its life, with nothing strong enough to stop the collapse.

cards.headline: Not a cosmic vacuum cleaner
cards.body: Black holes don’t suck everything in. From a safe distance, a black hole’s gravity is the same as that of any object with the same mass. If the Sun were swapped for a black hole of equal mass, the planets would keep orbiting just as they do now.
cards.callout: Same mass → same pull at a distance

cards.headline: Black holes: understood
learned: Nothing, not even light, escapes a black hole
Stellar black holes form from collapsing massive stars
At a distance, their gravity is like any equal mass

options.label: Nothing, not even light, can escape its gravity
It is made of dark rock
It is too far away to see
options.rationale: Distance isn’t what makes it black.

options.label: It is surrounded by dust clouds

questions.explanation: A black hole’s gravity is so strong that no light escapes, so it appears black.

questions.prompt: If the Sun were replaced by a black hole of the same mass, what would happen to Earth’s orbit?

options.label: Earth would be pulled in immediately
options.rationale: Its gravity at our distance would be unchanged.

options.label: Earth would fly off into space
options.rationale: The pull would stay the same.

options.label: Earth would stop orbiting and freeze in place

questions.explanation: At a distance, a black hole’s gravity equals that of any object with the same mass, so Earth’s orbit wouldn’t change, though it would get very cold.

questions.prompt: From Level 37: escape velocity is the speed needed to break free of gravity. What is true at a black hole?

options.label: Its escape velocity is about 11.2 km/s
Its escape velocity exceeds the speed of light
It has no escape velocity at all
Its escape velocity is lower than Earth’s

questions.explanation: Near a black hole, escaping would require going faster than light, which nothing can do.
